modules.name: Node canvas and typed, versioned ports
modules.design_question: Which browser node-canvas library and typed-port scheme lets designers wire Layer 0 and module outputs together accessibly, with type, unit, cycle and cardinality errors rejected on every edit path?
inputs: User edits: add, connect (click or drag), move, group, collapse, paste, undo/redo
Layer 0 payload type ids with version, dimension and unit (schema owner not yet named, see flags)
outputs: Graph document JSON: nodes {id, module@version, params, enabled}, edges {fromPort, toPort}, revision id
Port-type registry: versioned type id (e.g. layer0.geometry/v1) -> JSON Schema $id, dimension, unit
Connection-rejected events with the expected type, unit and reason
Outline/table view model of nodes, ports and edges

parameters.name: connection_rule (exact versioned type id | declared subtype | via converter node)
parameters.relationship: Stricter rule -> fewer invalid wires reach execution but more converter nodes. Ports carry type version plus physical dimension, so metre-to-foot or length-to-area wires need an explicit converter. React Flow lets the app veto UI connections (isValidConnection).

parameters.name: type_id_versioning (vN suffix, deprecation window)
parameters.relationship: A breaking change to a Layer 0 type creates a new id (layer0.geometry/v2); modules declare accepted versions, so old graphs fail loudly instead of mis-wiring silently. Owner and deprecation window are maintainer decisions (design logic, unsourced).

parameters.name: site_frame (units, local frame or CRS, grid_to_true_north_deg)
parameters.relationship: Sun, shadow and wind modules rotate the site frame by the grid-to-true-north angle; a missing or wrong angle casts shadows toward the wrong compass direction. The VTC site plan's north arrow is rotated against the street grid.

parameters.name: cycle_policy (reject in the graph model on every edit path)
parameters.relationship: A cycle -> no topological order exists, so the graph cannot execute. The check runs in the graph-model reducer, so paste, import, undo/redo and programmatic setEdges cannot create one either.

parameters.name: port_cardinality (item | list | tree)
parameters.relationship: Tree ports (path -> branch -> item) let one module evaluate many floors or towers in one run, as Grasshopper data trees do; the matching rule is set in P15-M02. Adds a concept users must learn.

parameters.name: canvas_library (xyflow | Rete | Baklava | litegraph)
parameters.relationship: A maintained library with a large user base lowers forced-migration risk; an archived or stale one raises it. Observed push dates and weekly downloads are in the metrics.

parameters.name: collapsed_groups (hidden flag) and onlyRenderVisibleElements
parameters.relationship: Collapsing node trees through the hidden property, or rendering only elements in the viewport, lowers the rendered node count and re-render cost on pan, zoom and edit; viewport rendering adds some overhead.

parameters.name: handle_hit_area (>= 24 CSS px at every zoom)
parameters.relationship: WCAG 2.5.8 is independent of page zoom. Canvas zoom (React Flow minZoom default 0.5) likely shrinks handles by the same factor (inference), so counter-scale the hit area or rely on the spacing exception.

parameters.name: non_drag_alternatives (click-to-connect, nudge buttons, numeric size fields)
parameters.relationship: Each drag action needs a single-pointer non-drag alternative: click source then target (connectOnClick, default on), nudge buttons, numeric fields. Keyboard is a separate criterion; React Flow documents focus and arrow-key moves, not keyboard connect.

metrics.name: Canvas interaction latency (scripted set, Event Timing p98)
metrics.method: Script drag, click-to-connect, parameter edit and run-all on the reference VTC graph in Chromium (Playwright). Record Event Timing durations and report the 98th percentile per session (as the web-vitals library does); Total Blocking Time is a secondary lab proxy.
metrics.basis: web.dev INP bands are defined for field data at the 75th percentile of page loads; lab INP depends on the scripted interactions and TBT is only a proxy. Earlier labelled 'verified' in error; now a team assumption borrowing the bands.

metrics.name: Pointer target size of handles and buttons
metrics.good: >= 24 x 24 CSS px at every zoom in range (or spacing exception)
metrics.bad: < 24 x 24 CSS px without an exception
metrics.method: Automated DOM measurement of every interactive element at minZoom, zoom 1 and maxZoom, plus manual review of the spacing exception (24 px circles must not intersect other targets).
metrics.basis: WCAG 2.2 SC 2.5.8 Target Size (Minimum), Level AA; the requirement is independent of page zoom.

metrics.name: Single-pointer non-drag alternative for every drag action
metrics.good: Connect, move and resize each work by click or tap without dragging
metrics.method: Checklist test with a single-pointer device: click-source-then-target connect, select-then-nudge or click-destination move, numeric resize fields.
metrics.basis: WCAG 2.2 SC 2.5.7 requires a pointer alternative; keyboard equivalence does not automatically meet it. Earlier metric said 'or keyboard alternative'. The understanding page does not mention node editors, so applying it here is our reading.

metrics.name: Keyboard operability of graph editing
metrics.good: Add, connect, disconnect, move, toggle and delete all work by keyboard with a defined focus order; outline view supports connect and disconnect
metrics.bad: Any editing function needs a mouse
metrics.method: Playwright keyboard-only script plus a screen-reader pass (NVDA or VoiceOver) on the outline view.
metrics.basis: WCAG 2.2 SC 2.1.1 Keyboard. React Flow documents Tab focus and arrow-key moves but not keyboard connect, so it is built here.

metrics.name: Non-text contrast of ports, wires and status chips
metrics.good: >= 3:1 against adjacent colours; ports also differ by shape or label
metrics.bad: < 3:1, or colour is the only cue
metrics.method: Automated contrast check of theme tokens in light and dark mode; manual check that port types are distinguishable without colour.
metrics.basis: WCAG 2.2 SC 1.4.11 Non-text Contrast, Level AA. The shape/label rule is a team design rule.

metrics.name: Invalid connections accepted by the model (any edit path)
metrics.method: Property test over UI wiring, paste, template import, undo/redo and programmatic setEdges: random port pairs must be accepted only when type, unit, cycle and cardinality rules allow.
metrics.basis: Course requirement that outputs are typed inputs of the next node; zero tolerance is our policy. isValidConnection guards only UI wiring, so the rule lives in the reducer.

metrics.name: Canvas library maintenance health
metrics.good: Not archived and pushed within 90 days
metrics.bad: Archived, or no push for more than 12 months
metrics.method: Read GitHub pushed_at and archived flag; npm weekly downloads for adoption. Observed 21 Oct 2026: xyflow pushed 2026-10-20 (8.35 M downloads/week); Rete pushed 2026-10-18 (47 k); Baklava pushed 2026-09-16 (1.7 k); litegraph.js pushed 2024-08-01; Comfy-Org litegraph fork archived (pushed 2026-01-14).
metrics.basis: Threshold days are an editable team preset; the observed values are verified.

metrics.name: Interactive node/edge capacity at 60 fps on a mid-range laptop
metrics.good: unverified: to be benchmarked
metrics.method: Benchmark with synthetic graphs of increasing size, with and without onlyRenderVisibleElements; React Flow's performance guide gives no node-count figures.
metrics.basis: No published sourced figure found.

visualization: The canvas: node cards with a category colour stripe (13 taxonomy codes), title, input ports left, output ports right, and a status badge (verified / team assumption / FALSE ASSUMPTION in its reserved colour).
Ports coloured and shaped by type (circle = item, square = list, diamond = tree) with a unit label and version chip; colour is never the only cue; collapsible legend.
A rejected connection shows a red dashed ghost wire and a tooltip such as 'expects layer0.geometry/v1 [m], got table [ft]'.
Outline/table view of every node, port and edge with connect and disconnect buttons and ARIA names such as 'Daylight node, input layer0.geometry/v1, connected from Massing'.
Minimap, collapsed group frames and an auto-layout button.
modules.method: Build on @xyflow/react. Custom nodes are generated from manifests (P15-M03); each Handle carries a versioned port-type id (a JSON Schema $id), dimension and unit. The graph JSON is the single source of truth; React Flow keeps only view state. Type, unit, cycle (walk getOutgoers from the target) and single-cardinality rules run in the graph-model reducer, so UI wiring (isValidConnection), paste, template import, undo/redo and setEdges share one check; P15-M02 re-checks at load. Click-to-connect, nudge buttons and an outline/table view give non-drag, keyboard and screen-reader paths. Handle hit areas are counter-scaled to stay at least 24 CSS px at every zoom. Memoise nodes, collapse groups with hidden, lay out with dagre. Keep the React Flow attribution visible unless a Pro subscription is bought.

modules.name: DAG execution, run-all vs step-into, provenance
modules.design_question: How does the tool run a wired graph reproducibly, let users run all or step into one node, and record inputs, thresholds, sources and environment so results show their work?
inputs: Per-node enabled flag and user threshold overrides
External datasets as hashed input nodes (content hash, retrieval date)
outputs: RunRecord JSON (RFC 8785 canonical): run_id, graph revision and hash, environment block {platform version, browser and engine, runtime versions, seed}, per node {module@version, parameter values, input hashes, outputs, metrics with threshold basis and source ids, status flag, duration, error, bypass stamp}
Typed node results consumed by downstream nodes
Stale/blocked status map for the canvas

parameters.name: execution_mode (auto | run-all | step-into)
parameters.relationship: Auto keeps results fresh but recomputes on every edit; run-all gives the user control over cost; step-into exposes one node's inputs, parameters and thresholds for audit. Design choice; no sourced evidence on trust effects.

parameters.name: cache_key = hash(module@version, parameters, upstream hashes, external-data hashes, seed, matching rule)
parameters.relationship: Same key -> reuse the cached output; changed key -> recompute that node and its descendants. Rete's dataflow engine caches outputs and needs an explicit reset when inputs change.

parameters.name: topological schedule (Kahn)
parameters.relationship: Ordering nodes so each runs after its inputs costs O(V+E); edges left over after the queue empties reveal a cycle, so a cyclic graph is refused.

parameters.name: cardinality and matching rule (item | list | tree; longest-list default; graft/flatten nodes)
parameters.relationship: Whether a module runs once or per branch depends on input structure. A list meeting an item input needs a declared matching rule, or run counts and hashes become ambiguous; the rule enters the cache key. Default is design logic.

parameters.name: disabled_node_mode (block default | bypass via declared passthrough ports)
parameters.relationship: Block marks every descendant blocked, so no verdict is computed on missing data. Bypass is allowed only through a manifest-declared passthrough port pair, and downstream results are stamped 'computed with X bypassed'. One enum for the whole tool (P15-M07 reuses it). Design logic.

parameters.name: timeout and cancel
parameters.relationship: Longer budget -> fewer false kills on heavy modules but a longer stall. Default cancel is Worker.terminate; a Pyodide SharedArrayBuffer interrupt needs cross-origin isolation headers and is optional.

parameters.name: threshold_override (editable team assumption)
parameters.relationship: Editing a threshold changes the cache key of every dependent node, so the new run is recorded with the value actually used.

parameters.name: numeric_tolerance (per-metric; exact hash only on the same engine and version)
parameters.relationship: ECMAScript lets engines approximate functions such as sin and exp, so last digits can differ across browsers. Compare across engines within a declared per-metric tolerance; compare exact canonical-JSON hashes only on the same engine and version.

parameters.name: external_data_inputs (hashed dataset nodes)
parameters.relationship: A dataset enters as an input node whose content hash and retrieval date join the cache key; a changed dataset gives a new key and a recompute, instead of a stale result that still looks complete.

metrics.name: Determinism (same engine and version)
metrics.good: 100% identical canonical-JSON hashes on two consecutive runs with the same inputs, versions and seed; across engines every numeric output within its declared tolerance
metrics.bad: Any same-engine hash difference, or a cross-engine difference beyond tolerance
metrics.method: Serialise with RFC 8785 (sorted keys, ECMAScript number formatting); run twice in CI on Chromium and Firefox; compare hashes per engine and values across engines within tolerance.
metrics.basis: Course requirement that results show their work; thresholds are our policy. Fixed-precision rounding is avoided because boundary values flip.

metrics.name: Provenance completeness
metrics.good: 100% of result values carry module@version, parameters, input hash, threshold basis, source id/status and the run's environment block (platform version, browser and engine, runtime versions, seed, external-data hashes and dates)
metrics.method: Schema check of every RunRecord entry.
metrics.basis: Course requirement: every result cites its source and shows its work.

metrics.name: Scheduling cost
metrics.good: O(V+E)
metrics.method: Kahn or DFS topological sort.
metrics.basis: Standard algorithm complexity.

metrics.name: Main-thread responsiveness during a run (Event Timing p98)
metrics.method: Run heavy modules in workers; during scripted run-all on the reference VTC graph record Event Timing durations and report p98 per session; Total Blocking Time as secondary proxy.
metrics.basis: INP bands (web.dev) are field p75 values for page loads; applying them to a lab run is our adaptation. Earlier labelled 'verified' in error.

metrics.name: Incremental re-run time after one parameter change
metrics.method: Wall-clock of re-run with warm cache on the reference VTC graph.
metrics.basis: Editable preset; no sourced benchmark.

metrics.name: Bypass/block stamp coverage
metrics.good: 100% of results downstream of a disabled node carry 'blocked' or 'computed with X bypassed' in the RunRecord and on the chip
metrics.method: Reachability test from every toggled node over the reference graph.
metrics.basis: Design policy so a pass/fail verdict never silently changes meaning.

visualization: Node status chips (idle, stale, running, ok, warn, error, blocked, bypassed) and a pulse travelling along wires during a run.
Bottom timeline (Gantt) of per-node durations.
Step-into side panel in three columns: Inputs (hash, preview) | Method, parameters, thresholds with source links | Outputs with pass/fail badges and the environment block.
Run-diff table between two RunRecords and a 'download provenance' button.
modules.method: Load the graph, validate it against manifests (P15-M03) and port rules (P15-M01), Kahn-sort it and refuse cycles. For each node compute the cache key; on a hit reuse the output, otherwise call the module runtime (first-party code or the T0 evaluator now; the P15-M04 sandbox later), validate inputs and outputs with Ajv, and append an entry to the RunRecord with the environment block. RunRecords are serialised as RFC 8785 canonical JSON. Run-all executes the full order; step-into shows a node's inputs, parameters and thresholds (read-only inspector first; pause-edit-resume later). A failed node blocks descendants. Disabled nodes follow the single toggle enum (block default; bypass only via declared passthrough, stamped downstream). Results are immutable; any edit makes a new run.

modules.human_judgment: The designer chooses which modules to enable, whether to override a threshold, and whether a pass/fail verdict means anything for the design; the tool only computes and logs.

Cache keys cannot see changes in undeclared external data. Step-into is our UX design, not a standard. Auto vs manual mode effects on user trust have no sourced evidence.
jury_criteria: No direct jury criterion; supports evidence traceability for all four tags (human_scale_40, cultural_context_30, design_excellence_20, urban_integration_10).

modules.name: Module manifest, T0 declarative modules and validator
modules.design_question: What manifest makes every module self-describing, source-cited, safely renderable and machine-checkable, so thresholds, assumptions, licences and visualization payloads are validated before a module can run or be published?
inputs: Taxonomy enumerations (13 category codes, 5 phases, 4 jury tags)
Source extracts and visualization payload samples
outputs: Validated manifest object
Port-type registry entries (versioned)
Lint report (errors and warnings)
Module-card data for palette, registry and review (P15-M05, P15-M06)
Visualization-payload validation result

parameters.name: id and name rules
parameters.relationship: A unique lowercase id keeps forks distinct and saved graphs resolvable. VS Code requires lowercase names, Obsidian a unique id, Yak restricted characters, crates.io case-insensitive collision checks.

parameters.name: version (SemVer 2.0.0; 0.y.z handling)
parameters.relationship: The number encodes change impact: a backward-incompatible schema change raises MAJOR. In 0.y.z anything may change, so a MINOR bump inside 0.x counts as breaking (^0.2.3 stays below 0.3.0), or listing requires 1.0.0.

parameters.name: category, phase, jury_tags (enumerations)
parameters.relationship: Category decides palette placement and colour; jury tags let a dashboard aggregate which criteria a graph evidences. VS Code similarly limits categories to a fixed list.

parameters.name: inputs / outputs as JSON Schema 2020-12, direction-aware diff
parameters.relationship: Typed ports derive from schemas. Narrowing an input, or widening an output, breaks consumers because they receive values they never handled; adding an optional output field is compatible. Design logic, unsourced.

parameters.name: parameters[] with relationship text, unit, source_ids
parameters.relationship: Making the causal relationship a required field stops a module from hiding assumptions; empty relationship -> lint error.

parameters.name: metrics[] with good, bad, status, source_ids
parameters.relationship: Status enum (verified | team_assumption | unverified | false_assumption_corrected) decides chip colour and whether a source is mandatory.

parameters.name: visualization contract (declarative payload types)
parameters.relationship: A module returns typed payloads (chart spec, grid, mesh, table, text) that first-party code renders; no HTML, SVG strings, URLs or expressions. Otherwise module markup is an XSS risk and image requests, governed by img-src, can carry data out.

parameters.name: output_caps (max bytes, list length, vertices)
parameters.relationship: Unbounded outputs can exhaust memory or freeze rendering; the manifest declares caps and the host enforces them at the message boundary. Numeric defaults await benchmarking.

parameters.name: source_extract_policy (max words, clause numbers)
parameters.relationship: Standards such as NBC/VBBL, ASHRAE and CSA are copyrighted: store clause numbers and derived numeric thresholds, never tables or clauses. Extract fields are capped (preset 25 words) so a manifest cannot reproduce long passages. Team policy, not legal advice.

parameters.name: t0_declarative_module (formula plus thresholds as data)
parameters.relationship: Most evaluation modules are a formula plus thresholds, so a JSON module run by a first-party evaluator needs no code execution. A restricted grammar limits risk; mathjs' own docs admit unknown parser vulnerabilities and advise a killable worker.

parameters.name: licence (SPDX expression)
parameters.relationship: The declared licence decides who may fork and redistribute; a missing licence means no reuse rights.

parameters.name: permissions[] and runtime tier (T0-T3)
parameters.relationship: Each declared permission widens what the sandbox grants; a new permission in an update forces re-approval, as Chrome does. T0 modules need none.

parameters.name: engines (platform version range)
parameters.relationship: Declares compatible platform versions so incompatible modules are not loaded, as VS Code's engines.vscode field does.

metrics.name: Manifest schema validity
metrics.good: 0 validation errors
metrics.method: Ajv validation at editor save, registry CI and graph load.
metrics.basis: CI gate policy; validator mechanism is standard JSON Schema.

metrics.name: Threshold classification coverage
metrics.good: 100% of thresholds have status verified (with at least one opened source), team_assumption, or unverified
metrics.bad: Any unclassified threshold, or verified without a source
metrics.method: Lint rule over metrics[].
metrics.basis: Course requirement: unsourced thresholds appear as editable team assumptions.

metrics.name: SemVer compliance
metrics.good: No breaking input/output schema diff without a MAJOR bump (a MINOR bump inside 0.y.z counts as the breaking bump)
metrics.bad: Breaking diff shipped as PATCH, or as MINOR at >= 1.0.0
metrics.method: Compare two manifest versions' schemas (removed or narrowed inputs, widened or retyped outputs) and compare with the bump.
metrics.basis: SemVer 2.0.0: backward-incompatible change -> MAJOR; 0.y.z is initial development where anything may change; released versions are immutable. The 0.x convention follows caret-range behaviour (team choice).

metrics.name: Direction-aware diff fixtures
metrics.good: Fixtures for input narrowing and output widening are both flagged breaking; an added optional output field is flagged compatible
metrics.method: Vitest fixtures with paired manifest versions.
metrics.basis: Design logic; no JSON Schema standard defines port variance.

metrics.name: Licence field validity
metrics.good: Valid SPDX expression; code licence is OSI-approved
metrics.method: Parse with spdx-expression-parse; check against the SPDX list with its OSI-approved flag.
metrics.basis: SPDX License List identifiers and OSI flag.

metrics.name: Source link health
metrics.good: All source URLs resolve at CI time
metrics.bad: Any 404 or 403 without an archived copy
metrics.method: HEAD requests in CI; opened flag recorded per source.
metrics.basis: Team policy; several sources in this packet returned 403, so a fallback is needed.

metrics.name: Test presence
metrics.good: >= 1 passing fixture per metric
metrics.method: Run fixtures in Vitest; compare outputs with expected values.
metrics.basis: JOSS requires an automated test suite or documented manual tests; a numeric coverage threshold is deliberately not set because none was sourced.

metrics.name: Visualization payload validity
metrics.good: 100% of payloads validate against the declarative schema and size caps, with 0 URL, markup or expression strings
metrics.bad: Any payload with a URL, markup or expression, or above caps
metrics.method: Ajv validation plus a string scan of payloads; Vega specs run only through the CSP-safe interpreter.
metrics.basis: Design policy to keep module output data-only; img-src governs image requests; the Vega interpreter avoids Function and eval.

metrics.name: Source extract length
metrics.good: <= 25 words per extract and no copied tables or clauses
metrics.bad: Longer extract, or a copied table or clause
metrics.method: CI length check plus a reviewer checklist item.
metrics.basis: Editable preset; copyright caution for standards text, not legal advice.

visualization: Manifest editor form with live inline validation (red/green).
Module card in the palette: category stripe, version, SPDX badge, tier badge, and a stacked bar counting verified / team assumption / unverified thresholds.
Per-threshold chip linked to its source; FALSE ASSUMPTION chips in the reserved colour with the old value struck through and the corrected value beside it.
Lint report grouped by severity, with a visualization-payload previewer.
modules.method: Define the manifest as a JSON Schema (2020-12) with enumerations for category (13 codes), phase (5), jury tags (4), metric status (4) and runtime tier (T0-T3). Validate with Ajv at editor save, registry CI (P15-M05) and graph load (P15-M02). Visualization outputs must match a declarative payload schema (chart subset with inline data, grid, mesh, table, text) and are drawn by first-party code; Vega specs use the CSP-safe interpreter. A manifest-diff tool compares versions direction-aware (input narrowing and output widening are breaking) and suggests a bump. Lint: opened source per verified threshold, relationship text, SPDX licence, declared permissions, fixture per metric, SemVer (0.y.z rules), unique id, capped source extracts. Until P15-M04 ships, only first-party and T0 modules run.

Standards-text rules are team policy, not legal advice. i18n, icons and dependency conflict resolution are not specified.

modules.name: Sandbox for community code and visualizations
modules.design_question: How can the platform run community module code, and show its output, without exposing user models, tokens or the host page to malicious or buggy code?
inputs: Module bundle and manifest (runtime tier, permissions, output caps)
Validated input payload (JSON or transferred ArrayBuffer)
Pinned runtime and wheel bytes with SHA-256
outputs: Schema-validated module output and declarative visualization payload
Telemetry {cpu_ms, peak_memory, terminated, denied_calls[]}
Permission-grant record per module@version

parameters.name: runtime_tier (T0 declarative | T1 JS in QuickJS-WASM or SES | T2 Pyodide, dev only | T3 server container)
parameters.relationship: Higher tier -> more expressive, larger attack surface. Pyodide is no security boundary: four of seven products in the Aug 2026 report got no code fix; shipped fixes left in-process Pyodide. Browser T2 is dev-only; T3 is the Python default.

parameters.name: granted_permissions (network, storage, geometry read/write)
parameters.relationship: Default-deny plus declared permissions: each added permission enlarges what a compromised module can read or exfiltrate. Chrome warns users and disables an extension until it accepts a newly added permission.

parameters.name: origin isolation (separate registrable domain; CSP sandbox header)
parameters.relationship: allow-scripts plus allow-same-origin on same-origin content can remove its own sandbox. Serve the sandbox from a separate registrable domain with response header 'Content-Security-Policy: sandbox allow-scripts' (opaque origin); a meta tag cannot set it.

parameters.name: csp_placement (on the sandbox document, not the worker)
parameters.relationship: Blob and data workers inherit the creating document's CSP, so the policy sits on the sandbox document's response header (default-src 'none'; script-src with blob: and 'wasm-unsafe-eval'; worker-src blob:; connect-src 'none'). Exact strings are CI-tested per tier.

parameters.name: header_capable_host
parameters.relationship: GitHub Pages cannot set response headers (the coi-serviceworker page says so), so the sandbox origin needs a host with a headers file, such as Cloudflare Pages _headers (up to 100 rules); the registry index can stay on Pages.

parameters.name: runtime_bytes_via_host
parameters.relationship: connect-src 'none' also stops a runtime fetching its own .wasm and packages. The host fetches pinned bytes, checks SHA-256 and transfers ArrayBuffers; micropip and network stay off; the manifest pins runtime and package list. Feasibility per runtime is untested.

parameters.name: memory, stack and time limits
parameters.relationship: Caps stop runaway modules; QuickJS offers memory, stack and interrupt-deadline limits, whereas SES does not mitigate memory or CPU exhaustion.

parameters.name: cross-origin isolation (COOP and COEP headers, optional)
parameters.relationship: Needed only for SharedArrayBuffer interrupts; default cancel is Worker.terminate. If used, apply COOP/COEP to the run page only, not module pages with cross-origin embeds such as giscus (inference); static hosts need a service-worker shim.

parameters.name: visualization_rendering (declarative payload, host-drawn)
parameters.relationship: Module markup in the host DOM is XSS, and image or CSS URLs can carry Layer 0 data out because img-src, not connect-src, governs them. Modules return declarative payloads (P15-M03); host code renders them; host CSP allowlists img-src and connect-src.

parameters.name: output_caps enforcement
parameters.relationship: Message-boundary checks reject outputs above manifest caps, so a module cannot exhaust host memory or rendering with huge arrays or meshes.

metrics.name: Sandbox-escape suite pass rate
metrics.good: 100% of red-team cases blocked per tier and browser (ctypes, Emscripten exports, fetch, XHR, WebSocket, DOM, storage, parent postMessage, eval, top navigation)
metrics.method: CI red-team suite per tier, seeded with the failure classes from the Aug 2026 Pyodide disclosure.
metrics.basis: Policy threshold; failure classes verified in the Cyera report (seven products affected, including n8n CVE-2025-68668).

metrics.name: Sandbox CSP delivered and denial verified cross-browser
metrics.good: Sandbox document carries the CSP and sandbox header; fetch, WebSocket, importScripts, nested Worker, eval and top navigation are denied in Chromium, Firefox and WebKit, and the blob worker starts
metrics.bad: Any call allowed, or the worker fails to start in any engine
metrics.method: Playwright tests on all three engines against the deployed sandbox origin.
metrics.basis: The earlier design put a CSP on a worker response inside an opaque-origin iframe on GitHub Pages; MDN says blob and data workers inherit the creator's CSP and Pages cannot send headers. Start of blob workers in opaque-origin iframes is unconfirmed.

metrics.name: Visualization containment
metrics.good: 0 module-supplied HTML, SVG, URL or style strings reach the host DOM or any network request
metrics.method: Red-team cases for img src, CSS url(), SVG, anchor navigation and oversized payloads; host CSP report-only logging.
metrics.basis: Design policy; img-src governs images, so a connect-src 'none' worker alone does not close this channel.

metrics.name: Permission least-privilege
metrics.good: Used permissions equal declared permissions
metrics.method: Instrument host API calls; compare with manifest.
metrics.basis: Chrome guidance to request only permissions the main function needs.

metrics.name: Runaway-module containment
metrics.good: Module killed within its budget; Event Timing p98 <= 200 ms during the kill test
metrics.bad: p98 > 500 ms or module not killable
metrics.method: Infinite-loop fixture; watchdog calls Worker.terminate, then removes the iframe.
metrics.basis: Terminate semantics from MDN. INP bands from web.dev are field p75 values; borrowing them for a lab test is a team assumption (earlier labelled verified).

metrics.name: Resource caps enforced
metrics.good: Memory, time and output caps set and enforced for every tier
metrics.method: Per-tier preset in platform config; numeric defaults set after benchmarking.
metrics.basis: SES explicitly leaves exhaustion unmitigated; QuickJS provides the knobs.

metrics.name: Pyodide cold-start time and download size
metrics.good: unverified: to be benchmarked
metrics.method: Measure first load and warm load on campus network; npm core package unpacked size is 13,879,282 bytes (core only).
metrics.basis: No sourced figure for end-to-end cold start.

metrics.name: Bundle provenance and integrity
metrics.good: 100% of community releases carry a GitHub artifact attestation verified in CI, and the client checks the index SHA-256 before loading
metrics.method: CI runs gh attestation verify; client verifies SHA-256 like subresource integrity.
metrics.basis: npm provenance applies to npm publish, not to file bundles at URLs. GitHub attestations link a bundle to its workflow and commit; they prove origin, not safety.

metrics.name: Python isolation boundary
metrics.good: Published community Python runs only in T3 (server or OS isolation); browser Pyodide is limited to unpublished dev use
metrics.bad: A published module runs in-page Pyodide without process or OS isolation
metrics.method: Registry CI rejects tier T2 for published listings.
metrics.basis: Cyera: four of seven products had no code fix; the fixes that shipped (n8n external runners, Grist Deno, smolagents removing WasmExecutor) left in-process Pyodide.

visualization: Install-time permission card in plain language with icons (reads geometry: yes; network: none; storage: none; CPU/memory caps) modelled on browser extension permission warnings.
Per-node runtime badge: tier T0-T3, shield colour for 'reviewed' vs 'unreviewed community', small live meters for CPU ms and memory.
Red 'terminated' banner with reason; amber 'payload rejected' banner naming the schema rule; sandbox report log with denied calls.
modules.method: Community T1 code runs in a blob Worker inside an iframe served from a separate registrable domain on a header-capable host. The iframe response header sets 'sandbox allow-scripts' plus a CSP (default-src 'none'; script-src 'self' blob: 'wasm-unsafe-eval'; worker-src blob:; connect-src 'none'; img-src 'none'), inherited by the blob worker. The host fetches pinned runtime bytes (SHA-256 checked) and talks to the worker only by postMessage with schema, size and count checks. Output is data plus a declarative visualization payload drawn by host code; module markup never enters the host DOM. A watchdog calls Worker.terminate, then removes the iframe. T1: QuickJS-WASM or SES; T2: browser Pyodide (dev only); T3: gVisor/microVM server job, the default for published Python. CI red-team suite per tier in Chromium, Firefox, WebKit.

modules.name: Registry and distribution
modules.design_question: How should modules be published, reviewed, versioned, forked, verified and installed so the community can share them GitHub-style while maintainers keep quality and security?
inputs: Pull request adding a module version (manifest, bundle, tests)
Maintainer review decisions and CI results
outputs: Registry index: one JSON-lines file per module id, one line per version {version, bundle URL, SHA-256, attestation, dependency ranges, tier, permissions, yanked, reason, forked_from}
Installable bundles with GitHub artifact attestations, mirrored by the registry
flags.json kill-switch list read by clients
Fork lineage graph and workspace lockfile entries

parameters.name: index_model (git index repo | sparse static JSON)
parameters.relationship: A git index gives reviewable history and zero server cost; sparse per-file fetching lowers client download. Cargo supports both; Homebrew taps are plain git repositories installed by name.

parameters.name: review_gate (CI plus human approval)
parameters.relationship: Homebrew merges only after CI passes and an organisation member approves; Obsidian review is automated and blocks installation until errors are fixed; Yak describes no review step. Stricter gate -> higher quality, slower publishing.

parameters.name: immutability and yank
parameters.relationship: A published version is never edited; yanking sets a flag so new installs skip it while existing pinned graphs still resolve (Cargo yanked flag; Comfy and Yak versions cannot be overwritten).

parameters.name: version resolution and lockfile
parameters.relationship: Exact pins in the lockfile keep results reproducible; ranges apply to dependencies only, and 0.y.z caret ranges stay inside one minor (^0.2.3 < 0.3.0). ComfyUI stores node versions in workflow JSON for the same reason.

parameters.name: fork lineage (forked_from)
parameters.relationship: A fork is a separate repository linked to upstream, and forks of public repositories are public, so entrants cannot fork the index privately. Track lineage through forked_from plus a CI licence-compatibility check.

parameters.name: naming and namespace
parameters.relationship: Case-insensitive collision checks and treating '-' and '_' as equal reduce confusing or look-alike names (crates.io rules).

parameters.name: bundle_integrity (SHA-256 + attestation + mirror)
parameters.relationship: The index stores a SHA-256 and attestation reference per bundle; the client verifies the hash before loading and CI verifies the attestation. Attestations prove where a bundle was built, not that it is safe; accepted bundles are mirrored.

parameters.name: client_kill_switch (flags.json)
parameters.relationship: Clients fetch flags.json at start and refuse or warn on yanked or blocked versions already in a lockfile, showing the reason; without it a malicious version stays loadable in saved graphs.

parameters.name: hosting limits
parameters.relationship: GitHub Pages allows a 1 GB published site and a 100 GB/month soft bandwidth limit; larger assets such as Python wheels must come from a CDN.

metrics.name: CI gate before merge
metrics.good: 100% of merged module PRs passed all automated checks
metrics.method: Branch protection requires status checks and a CODEOWNERS review.
metrics.basis: Homebrew contributing guide: pull requests with failing CI should not be merged.

metrics.name: Time to first maintainer response
metrics.good: <= 3 days
metrics.method: Median interval from PR open to first non-bot response.
metrics.basis: Editable preset; CHAOSS defines the metric and says to exclude bot replies but gives no numeric bands.

metrics.name: SemVer breaking-change detection
metrics.good: Every schema-breaking change shipped as MAJOR (MINOR inside 0.y.z)
metrics.bad: Breaking change shipped as PATCH, or as MINOR at >= 1.0.0
metrics.method: Automated direction-aware manifest diff in CI (P15-M03).
metrics.basis: SemVer 2.0.0 items 4 and 8.

metrics.name: Published registry size
metrics.good: <= 1 GB
metrics.method: Measure the Pages artifact in CI.
metrics.basis: GitHub Pages published-site limit.

metrics.name: Bundles with verified attestation and matching SHA-256
metrics.method: CI runs gh attestation verify before the index line is accepted; client integration test checks the hash.
metrics.basis: Earlier cited npm provenance, which applies only to npm publish. GitHub artifact attestations (actions/attest) apply to build artifacts such as bundles; threshold is our policy.

metrics.name: Flagged or yanked versions shown with reason in the client
metrics.method: Client integration test against flags.json and the yanked field.
metrics.basis: Course requirement that wrong claims stay visible.

metrics.name: Time to block a reported malicious version in clients
metrics.good: <= 2 days
metrics.method: Interval from a verified report to a flags.json entry live in clients.
metrics.basis: Editable preset; no sourced benchmark.

visualization: Registry grid with filters by category code, phase, jury tag, licence, tier and status; cards show version, SPDX badge, tests pass/fail, counts of verified and team-assumption thresholds, attestation tick, expert-reviewed badge.
Module detail page: README, manifest summary, source list, version timeline with yanked and FALSE ASSUMPTION markers, dependents.
Fork lineage drawn as a DAG; PR review checklist sidebar with CI status badges.
Install button adds module@version to the workspace lockfile; blocked versions show a red banner with the reason.
modules.method: The registry is a public GitHub repository (index repo) with one JSON-lines file per module id and one line per version, following the Cargo index layout. An author opens a PR adding a version line {version, bundle URL, SHA-256, attestation, dependency ranges, tier, permissions, forked_from}. CI runs manifest lint (P15-M03), fixtures, the sandbox red-team smoke test (P15-M04), the SPDX check, the source-link check and attestation verification (gh attestation verify). A CODEOWNERS maintainer approves; merge publishes the index through GitHub Pages and mirrors the bundle. Bundles are built by GitHub Actions with actions/attest. Clients verify SHA-256, resolve exact versions into a workspace lockfile and fetch flags.json at start. Yanking flips a flag; other fields never change. Nothing from a user's project is uploaded here (P15-M07).

modules.limits: A static registry has no server-side rate limiting or private modules; Pages bandwidth is a soft cap; the PR queue is a maintainer bottleneck. Attestations prove where a bundle was built, not that it is safe. Whether release assets can be replaced under the same name, and attestation eligibility by plan, were not verified. Food4Rhino could not be opened.

modules.name: Comments, reviews, ratings and flags
modules.design_question: How do users comment on, review, rate and flag modules or single thresholds so wrong assumptions stay visible and ratings are not misleading, without exposing entrants' unpublished designs?
inputs: Discussion threads on registry module pages (GitHub Discussions via giscus)
Flag submissions {module@version, threshold id, claim, evidence URL, proposed correction, flag type}
outputs: Rating summary {n, positive fraction, Wilson lower bound}
Flag records with status, affected versions and corrected value
Chip colour state per threshold; moderation queue

parameters.name: rating_score (Wilson lower bound, z = 1.96)
parameters.relationship: Small samples inflate plain averages; the lower bound ranks 2 of 2 positive ratings at about 0.34 and 180 of 200 at about 0.85 (computed from the formula), so thinly rated modules do not outrank well-tested ones.

parameters.name: min_votes_to_display
parameters.relationship: Below a minimum n the interval is wide, so show 'not enough ratings' instead of a number.

parameters.name: vote_integrity (one vote per GitHub account per major version)
parameters.relationship: Votes parsed from replies are easy to game with several replies or later edits; counting one vote per account per major version and ignoring post-aggregation edits limits inflation. Design logic; n >= 5 is still a thin floor.

parameters.name: flag_taxonomy (FALSE_ASSUMPTION | UNVERIFIED | UNRESOLVED | TEAM_ASSUMPTION)
parameters.relationship: A flagged claim is never deleted; the record keeps affected versions and the fixed version, as OSV records introduced, fixed and withdrawn events for advisories.

parameters.name: discussion_backend (giscus on GitHub Discussions | own database)
parameters.relationship: giscus stores threads in GitHub Discussions and needs no database, but the repository must be public and users need GitHub accounts, so every thread is public and identity-linked. An own database removes that at the cost of hosting and moderation.

parameters.name: discussion_scope_and_embargo
parameters.relationship: Public, identity-linked threads can expose an entrant's scheme before judging (VTC terms 4.1, 5.1, 5.3). Threads attach to registry module pages only, entrants are told not to discuss their own scheme before results, and none is embedded in project or template views.

parameters.name: moderator_response_time
parameters.relationship: Longer time to first response -> lower perceived activity and weaker contributor retention (CHAOSS objective; no numeric relationship given).

parameters.name: expert vs crowd separation
parameters.relationship: Crowd ratings measure perceived usefulness; expert review (P15-M08) measures correctness. Showing them separately, and never beside the verified-status chip, prevents a popular but wrong module looking verified. Design logic.

metrics.name: Wilson lower-bound rating
metrics.method: Count positive and negative votes; apply the Wilson score formula at 95% confidence.
metrics.basis: Formula and z = 1.96 verified; the good/bad cut-offs and minimum n are editable team presets.

metrics.name: Time to first response to comments and flags
metrics.good: <= 3 days
metrics.method: CHAOSS Time to First Response, excluding bot replies.
metrics.basis: Definition verified; bands are presets.

metrics.name: Flag completeness
metrics.good: Every FALSE_ASSUMPTION flag has evidence URL, corrected value and affected version range
metrics.method: Issue form validation plus maintainer checklist.
metrics.basis: Modelled on the OSV schema fields.

metrics.name: Flag visibility
metrics.good: 100% of flags render in their reserved colour with an icon and text label
metrics.method: UI test; contrast of the flag colour at least 3:1.
metrics.basis: Course requirement (flagged claims stay visible); WCAG non-text contrast.

metrics.name: Vote integrity
metrics.good: 1 counted vote per GitHub account per module major version; edits after aggregation ignored
metrics.method: Aggregation Action de-duplicates by account and major version; replay test with duplicate and edited replies.
metrics.basis: Design policy against gaming.

metrics.name: Public-thread exposure of unpublished designs
metrics.good: 0 threads or comments on project or template views before VTC results; module-page threads carry the 'do not discuss your own scheme' notice
metrics.method: UI test of where the giscus embed can load; notice present on every module page.
metrics.basis: Earlier text said repository visibility was unverified. giscus states the repository must be public, so all comments are public and tied to GitHub accounts.

visualization: Per-threshold chip: green verified, amber team assumption, grey unverified, reserved magenta-red FALSE ASSUMPTION with the old value struck through and the corrected value beside it; hover shows the source and flag history.
Rating histogram with a Wilson-interval whisker and an 'n' label, placed apart from the status chips.
Version strip showing affected and fixed version range, in OSV style.
Embedded giscus thread under each registry module page with a visible privacy notice; moderation queue for maintainers.
modules.method: Each registry module page embeds a giscus thread mapped to the module id; threads are for module feedback, and entrants are told not to discuss their own scheme before results. Structured reviews are replies using a template (vote plus evidence link); a GitHub Action parses them into ratings.json, counting one vote per account per major version and ignoring later edits. Ratings use the Wilson lower bound (z = 1.96), hidden below the minimum n. Flags come from an Issue form recording {module@version, threshold id, claim, evidence URL, proposed value, type}. Maintainers set status; an Action writes flags.json in the registry and never deletes entries. The client overlays flags on threshold chips; a confirmed false claim keeps the old value struck through and links to the corrected version. Expert badges are separate (P15-M08). Ships after 30 Nov.

GitHub API rate limits were not verified. COEP require-corp on a page embedding the cross-origin giscus iframe would likely block it (inference). Colour alone is insufficient; icons and text are required.

modules.name: Local-first projects, VTC-safe sharing and workflow templates
modules.design_question: How do projects stay private by default, templates get shared safely after the VTC embargo, module versions get pinned, and modules switch on or off without silently breaking downstream results?
inputs: User on/off choices and embargo setting
outputs: Local project store with revision history
Template package: graph.json, lockfile.json, README, LICENSE, preview.svg, requires.json (Layer 0 port types, units)
Enabled-state map and dependency-impact report
Publish-gate decisions and a log of any design data leaving the device
Anonymity scan report for board exports

parameters.name: storage_model (local-first OPFS/IndexedDB, no server copy by default)
parameters.relationship: Design data stay in the browser, so unpublished visuals are not reachable by others. OPFS is origin-bound and is deleted when site data are cleared, so export and backup are mandatory; it is not synced across devices as far as MDN states.

parameters.name: publish_gate (warning on every off-device action until results)
parameters.relationship: VTC terms 4.1 require visuals not previously published and 5.1/5.3 require no identifying marks, so publish, fork, share, template upload and comment embeds warn first. The gate is a warning, not legal advice; 'published' is undefined in the terms.

parameters.name: template_export_scope (graph, parameters and pins by default; geometry, renders, outputs opt-in)
parameters.relationship: Geometry and renders reveal the scheme while module pins and parameters mostly do not, so only the latter export by default; the rest need explicit opt-in and an embargo date. Previews are drawn from graph JSON, not screenshots. Design logic.

parameters.name: collaboration_model (single writer + file merge | CRDT)
parameters.relationship: A 2-4 person team editing one graph needs merging. A CRDT such as Yjs merges concurrent edits and persists offline, but y-webrtc still needs signalling servers, and any relay sees data unless encrypted.

parameters.name: revision_history (undo/redo, revision id per RunRecord)
parameters.relationship: Each graph revision gets an id and each RunRecord stores it, so users can see which graph produced which numbers; undo creates a new revision and never edits a past record. Design logic.

parameters.name: lockfile pins (module@exact version)
parameters.relationship: Pinning keeps results reproducible when a module later changes; ComfyUI stores node versions in workflow JSON so workflows can be reproduced.

parameters.name: toggle semantics (the single enum of P15-M02)
parameters.relationship: Block is the default; bypass only through a declared passthrough pair, with downstream results stamped. Delete is an edit, not a toggle. Mixed semantics would change what a downstream pass/fail means. Design logic.

parameters.name: template licence
parameters.relationship: Graph JSON and docs are content (CC BY 4.0 suits); code keeps an OSI licence. Creative Commons advises against CC licences for software.

parameters.name: embedded third-party material
parameters.relationship: Never embed the brief, site model or Buildner presentation template package: 7.5.5 forbids redistributing the templates, 7.5.6 keeps the organiser's IP, and no licence for the brief is stated. Link and cite instead.

parameters.name: export_anonymity (metadata, filenames, visible names)
parameters.relationship: Board exports must not carry author or team marks (terms 5.1) and panels are JPEG files up to 10 MB (4.8). Metadata scans catch EXIF/XMP and PDF fields; OCR catches visible names that metadata scans miss.

metrics.name: Design data leaving the device before 30 Nov without opt-in
metrics.good: 0 bytes of project payload sent to any non-local origin
metrics.method: Playwright network-log assertion over a full session including undo, export and template flows.
metrics.basis: Policy derived from VTC terms 4.1, 5.1 and 5.3 (risk of identification or prior publication); not legal advice.

metrics.name: Publish-gate coverage
metrics.good: 100% of off-device actions (publish, fork, share link, template upload, comment embed) show the gate until results
metrics.method: Enumerate off-device code paths; UI test each.
metrics.basis: Policy.

metrics.name: Template reproducibility
metrics.good: 100% identical output hashes on re-run with pinned versions on the same engine
metrics.method: Import template, resolve lockfile, run twice, compare RunRecords.
metrics.basis: Course requirement of showing work; threshold is our policy.

metrics.name: Dependency resolvability
metrics.good: 100% of pinned modules resolve; yanked versions warned
metrics.method: Resolve each pin against the registry index.
metrics.basis: Policy; yank semantics from Cargo index.

metrics.name: Unwired required inputs
metrics.method: Static graph check against manifests.
metrics.basis: Policy.

metrics.name: Unmarked descendants after toggling off
metrics.method: Reachability from the toggled node; all descendants must show blocked or a bypass stamp.
metrics.basis: Policy.

metrics.name: Identifying strings in exports (metadata and visible text)
metrics.good: 0 in JPEG EXIF/XMP, PDF metadata, filenames, and OCR text
metrics.method: Scan exported JPEG panels and PDFs for author, team, institution and path strings; OCR pass for visible names.
metrics.basis: VTC 5.1 forbids identifying marks; the metadata scan and OCR are our implementation of it (earlier labelled verified in error).

metrics.name: Third-party brief or template files inside template packages
metrics.method: Hash and filename scan against the VTC downloads and the Buildner template package.
metrics.basis: Earlier text said the terms restrict nothing on redistribution; 7.5.5 forbids redistributing the Presentation Template Package and 7.5.6 keeps organiser IP.

visualization: Privacy indicator on the project header: 'Data on this device only', with last export time.
Publish-gate dialog listing exactly what would leave the device and the VTC terms it touches.
Template gallery cards: graph thumbnail, jury-tag dots, module count, licence badge; template detail with dependency list, lock status and flag chips.
On/off switch on every node; on toggle, descendants turn hatched with a banner 'n results depend on this module'; graph diff view for forks and merges.
modules.method: Projects live in the browser (OPFS/IndexedDB); nothing is uploaded unless the user opts in. A template is an archive of graph.json (modules at exact versions, parameters, enabled flags, edges), lockfile.json, README, LICENSE, preview.svg and requires.json; geometry, renders and RunRecord outputs are excluded unless opted in, with an embargo until VTC results. Every action that sends design data off the device (publish, fork, share, template upload, comment embed) first shows the VTC gate. Import resolves pins against the registry, warns on yanked or flagged versions (P15-M06) and lints (P15-M03). Toggling applies the single enum in P15-M02; the UI marks descendants by reachability. Board export strips author, team and path metadata, scans JPEG EXIF/XMP and PDF metadata, runs OCR for visible names, and draws graph images from JSON, not canvas screenshots.

What counts as 'previously published' under VTC 4.1 is undefined, so the gate is a warning, not advice. OCR cannot catch every identifying mark. No sourced evidence on best template granularity.

modules.name: Governance, licensing and expert-reviewed badge
modules.design_question: What contribution rules, code of conduct, maintainer roles, licences and expert-review process keep the open-source tool trustworthy, lawful, and respectful of Indigenous and copyright constraints?
inputs: Licence declarations from manifests and dependency trees
outputs: Governance documents: CONTRIBUTING, CODE_OF_CONDUCT, GOVERNANCE, SECURITY, LICENSE and content-licence matrix
Community-health checklist and Scorecard result
Review records {module@version, reviewers, expertise, thread URL, date} driving the badge

parameters.name: governance_model (BDFL | meritocracy | liberal contribution)
parameters.relationship: A small student-run project can start with named maintainers and a written contributor process, formalising later; documenting how someone becomes a maintainer in GOVERNANCE.md reduces the 'private clique' perception.

parameters.name: code_of_conduct text, version and reporting route
parameters.relationship: Contributor Covenant 3.0 is CC BY-SA 4.0, so derived texts must share alike; it needs a real contact and an enforcement ladder. Use a role mailbox plus a backup recipient (e.g. course staff), not one student's address.

parameters.name: code vs content licence
parameters.relationship: Code under an OSI-approved licence (MIT or Apache-2.0); documentation and templates under CC BY 4.0. Creative Commons recommends against CC licences for software and allows them for documentation and artistic elements.

parameters.name: review depth for the expert-reviewed badge
parameters.relationship: rOpenSci uses two external reviewers in a public thread; JOSS checks OSI licence, tests and documentation. More reviewers -> more confidence but longer lead time; the optimal number has no evidence.

parameters.name: CODEOWNERS and branch protection
parameters.relationship: Requiring a code-owner review makes an owner of each path approve changes to it; owners need write access or their approval is not requested.

parameters.name: AI-use disclosure
parameters.relationship: Homebrew requires disclosure of AI/LLM use and personal accountability for generated content; JOSS has an AI policy for reviews.

parameters.name: indigenous_data_hold_rule
parameters.relationship: CARE (collective benefit, authority to control, responsibility, ethics) puts Indigenous Peoples in charge of data about them. Hard rule: nothing representing Musqueam, Squamish or Tsleil-Waututh cultural knowledge is listed without documented Nation-authorised involvement; students never self-certify consent.

parameters.name: cultural_context_30 tag disclaimer
parameters.relationship: The tag says a module evidences that criterion, not that any Nation endorses it. Reviewers assign it, it is never self-assigned, and its card carries a no-endorsement notice. Design logic, unsourced.

parameters.name: advisory_route (UBC SALA and Nation protocols)
parameters.relationship: Nation-specific protocols and OCAP (FNIGC) could not be read (403). BC's DRIPA applies UNDRIP to provincial laws but does not bind a student project. An advisory route via UBC SALA is proposed, unconfirmed; until agreed, such content stays held.

parameters.name: brief and third-party redistribution
parameters.relationship: VTC 7.5.5 forbids redistributing the Presentation Template Package and 7.5.6 keeps organiser IP; no licence for the brief or site model is stated. Treat all as all-rights-reserved (team assumption); store citations and derived parameters only.

parameters.name: standards_text_policy
parameters.relationship: NBC/VBBL, ASHRAE and CSA documents are copyrighted: modules cite clause numbers and store derived thresholds; reviewers reject copied tables or clauses; manifest extracts are length-capped (P15-M03). Team policy, not legal advice.

parameters.name: vulnerability_disclosure_and_takedown
parameters.relationship: SECURITY.md names a private reporting channel; a confirmed malicious version is yanked and pushed to clients through flags.json (P15-M05). Response targets are editable presets.

sources.title: Pyodide - Keyboard interrupts
sources.extract: Interrupt with a SharedArrayBuffer passed to setInterruptBuffer; must run in a worker; server must send the headers SharedArrayBuffer requires.

sources.title: Sandcastles, Not Sandboxes: How One Architectural Flaw Exposed Seven Products
sources.extract: Published 7 Aug 2026: Python-level denylists in Pyodide sandboxes missed ctypes and Emscripten exports. Status table: n8n (CVE-2025-68668, CVSS 9.9) fixed by external runners; Grist fixed by moving to Deno; smolagents removed its opt-in WasmExecutor; cohere-terrarium ctypes path unpatched and repository archived; langchain-sandbox archived, no fix described; stlite and cibuildwheel made no code changes (deployer responsibility). Mitigations: allowlist, strip exports, OS-level isolation, least privilege; Python controls are not the sole boundary.

sources.title: MDN - Using Web Workers
sources.extract: Workers are in general not governed by the CSP of the creating document; an eval example shows a worker can use eval when the page cannot. Exception: if the worker script's origin is a globally unique identifier (data or blob URL) it inherits the creator's CSP. A worker's own CSP comes from a header on its script response. The page does not mention sandboxed iframes.

sources.title: MDN - iframe element (sandbox attribute)
sources.extract: Without allow-same-origin content gets a unique opaque origin; allow-scripts plus allow-same-origin on same-origin content lets it remove the sandbox; serve untrusted content from a separate origin.

sources.title: MDN - Window.crossOriginIsolated
sources.extract: Cross-origin isolation requires COOP same-origin and COEP require-corp or credentialless; needed to use SharedArrayBuffer.

sources.title: MDN - Worker.terminate()
sources.extract: Immediately stops a Web Worker without letting it finish pending operations.

sources.title: WebAssembly - Security
sources.extract: Modules run in fault-isolated sandboxes with bounds-checked linear memory and control-flow integrity; side channels, race conditions and overflows within linear memory remain possible.

sources.title: SES (Secure ECMAScript) - Endo
sources.extract: lockdown() freezes intrinsics; Compartments start with no ambient authority; limits: guests can run forever and allocate unlimited memory; availability and exhaustion threats not mitigated. Repository licence shown as Apache-2.0.

sources.title: quickjs-emscripten
sources.extract: QuickJS compiled to WebAssembly; memory limits, stack limits and interrupt/deadline handlers; host functions exposed explicitly; MIT per npm.

sources.title: Deno - Security and permissions
sources.extract: Default-deny permissions; --allow-run and --allow-ffi are equivalent to allow-all; for untrusted code use layered defence: minimal permissions, Web Worker, OS sandboxing, and gVisor or Firecracker VMs.

sources.title: coi-serviceworker

flags.claim: Pyodide/WebAssembly isolation is enough to run untrusted community Python safely in the browser.
flags.correction: Treat Pyodide as one layer only. A 7 Aug 2026 disclosure showed escapes in seven products (ctypes and Emscripten exports reached the JS host). Add host-level isolation (separate origin, CSP on the sandbox document, no network), allowlists, stripped exports, maintainer review, or run server-side in a sandbox.
flags.detail: WebAssembly's own docs list side channels and in-memory overflows as remaining risks; two of the seven products received no fix because maintainers treated isolation as the deployer's job (corrected in r1: four of seven got no code fix, see below).

flags.claim: A Web Worker created by our page inherits the page's Content-Security-Policy and is therefore a safe place for community code.
flags.correction: Workers are generally not governed by the creating document's CSP; a worker script must be served with its own CSP header (blob: and data: workers inherit). Workers also still have network access unless blocked.
flags.detail: MDN: a page with script-src 'self' blocks eval(), yet code in a worker it creates can still call eval().

flags.claim: litegraph.js (or its Comfy fork) is a maintained, safe choice for the node canvas.
flags.correction: Original litegraph.js last pushed 2024-08-01 with about 1.2 k weekly downloads; the Comfy-Org fork is archived (2026-01-14). Use @xyflow/react (pushed 2026-10-20, about 8.3 M weekly downloads) with Rete as the fallback.
flags.detail: Observed 21 Oct 2026 from GitHub API and npm download API.

flags.claim: A keyboard alternative satisfies the drag requirement ('Single-pointer or keyboard alternative to drag', WCAG 2.5.7).
flags.correction: Provide single-pointer, non-drag alternatives (click source then target, select then nudge or click destination, numeric size fields) and test keyboard operability separately under SC 2.1.1.
flags.detail: The Understanding page states that keyboard equivalence does not automatically meet SC 2.5.7 and that the two are evaluated independently (opened 21 Oct 2026, P15-S50). Affected metric: P15-M01 'Single-pointer non-drag alternative for every drag action'.

flags.claim: A sandboxed community worker can carry its own CSP response header (connect-src none) inside an opaque-origin iframe, with the sandbox hosted on GitHub Pages.
flags.correction: Put the CSP and the sandbox directive on the sandbox iframe document's response header, on a header-capable separate domain; the blob worker inherits it. Test denial of fetch, WebSocket, importScripts, nested Worker, eval and top navigation in Chromium, Firefox and WebKit.
flags.detail: MDN: blob and data workers inherit the creating document's CSP; only a worker with a normal URL uses its own response header (P15-S18). The coi-serviceworker page notes GitHub Pages cannot set headers (P15-S27). That an opaque-origin document can only start blob or data workers is an inference from same-origin worker fetch rules; the HTML spec page read stopped before the constructor steps, so it stays unverified.

flags.claim: INP thresholds are 'verified' for measuring canvas interaction latency in a test build at the 75th percentile.
flags.correction: Reclassified as team_assumption. Use a scripted interaction set and report Event Timing p98 per session, with Total Blocking Time as a secondary lab proxy.
flags.detail: web.dev defines the bands at the 75th percentile of field page loads; lab INP depends on which interactions are scripted; per visit INP is the longest interaction ignoring outliers, and web-vitals uses the 98th percentile (P15-S47). Affected metrics: P15-M01, P15-M02, P15-M04.

flags.claim: The VTC terms say nothing that restricts redistribution of competition materials, and only anonymity constrains entrants' publishing.
flags.correction: Never host Buildner's Presentation Template Package in modules or templates. Treat sharing design visuals before judging as a risk under 4.1, and keep projects local by default.
flags.detail: Terms 7.5.5 forbid redistribution, resale or sharing of the template package; 7.5.6 keeps the organiser's IP; 4.1 says visual materials must not have been previously published; the resubmission page requires previously published visuals to be visually updated (P15-S60, P15-S80). The terms have no clause on posting entries to social media, and 'published' is undefined.

flags.claim: Whether giscus needs a public repository is unknown.
flags.correction: giscus requires a public repository with the giscus app installed and Discussions enabled, so all comments are public and tied to GitHub accounts; module-page threads only, with a privacy notice.
flags.detail: giscus.app states the repository must be public, otherwise visitors cannot view the discussion (P15-S64). The earlier UNVERIFIED flag is resolved by this.

flags.claim: npm provenance provides signed provenance for registry module bundles.
flags.correction: Use GitHub artifact attestations (actions/attest) on bundle files, verify them in CI with gh attestation verify, and have the client check the index SHA-256; mirror accepted bundles.
flags.detail: npm provenance is generated by npm publish --provenance for packages on the npm registry; bundles at URLs in a JSON-lines index are not npm packages (P15-S40). GitHub attestations link a file to its workflow and commit and prove origin, not safety (P15-S70, P15-S71).

flags.claim: Two of the seven products in the Aug 2026 Pyodide disclosure received no fix.
flags.correction: Four of seven (cohere-terrarium, langchain-sandbox, stlite, cibuildwheel) had no code fix; the three fixes that shipped (n8n external runners, Grist Deno, smolagents removing WasmExecutor) moved or removed in-process Pyodide. Make T3 the Python default and keep browser Pyodide as a dev tier.
flags.detail: Cyera status table read 21 Oct 2026 (P15-S17): cohere-terrarium ctypes path unpatched and archived; langchain-sandbox archived with no fix described; stlite and cibuildwheel made no code changes.

flags.claim: MIT licensing of React Flow means the on-canvas attribution can be removed without paying.
flags.detail: The vendor states attribution may be removed only with a Pro subscription (Starter $169/month, Professional $289/month) while the library itself stays MIT. Whether MIT legally obliges the on-canvas badge was not verified; default is to leave it visible. Board and template images are drawn by our own SVG exporter, so no canvas badge is baked in; whether exports need the badge is also unverified.

flags.claim: The Contributor Covenant text is CC BY 4.0.
flags.correction: Version 3.0 is stated on its own page to be CC BY-SA 4.0 (share-alike). The 2.1 page opened in r1 states no licence at all. Decision: adopt 3.0 with a CC BY-SA attribution notice.
flags.detail: CC BY 4.0 for 2.1 was seen only in a search snippet, not on an opened primary page (P15-S83 states no licence); the 2.1 licence stays unverified but is moot once 3.0 is adopted.

flags.claim: Editable presets without literature source: INP bands applied to a canvas editor (Event Timing p98); incremental re-run <= 5 s good / > 30 s bad; time to first response <= 3 d good / > 14 d bad; time to block a malicious version <= 2 d good / > 7 d bad; Wilson score >= 0.80 good / < 0.50 bad with n >= 5; Scorecard >= 7 good / < 4 bad; library 'maintained' = pushed within 90 days; source extracts <= 25 words; expert badge needs >= 2 reviewers; output caps and cross-engine tolerances to be set after benchmarking.
flags.detail: Shown in the tool as editable team assumptions per the course rule; replace with sourced values when found.

flags.claim: React Flow node/edge capacity at 60 fps; Pyodide cold-start time; COEP side effects on third-party embeds (giscus, tiles); GitHub API rate limits; handle shrinkage under canvas zoom; mutability of GitHub release assets; attestation availability by plan.
flags.detail: No sourced figures found; each needs a benchmark or a read of the relevant documentation. The giscus repository-visibility question was resolved in r1 (public required).

flags.claim: A blob Worker can be started inside an opaque-origin sandboxed iframe in Chromium, Firefox and WebKit, and 'wasm-unsafe-eval' is enough CSP for QuickJS-WASM and Pyodide.
flags.detail: MDN confirms the CSP inheritance, the sandbox header and the wasm-unsafe-eval keyword, but not worker creation from an opaque origin or the minimum CSP of each runtime. The CI denial suite decides; fallback design B serves the sandbox page on a separate registrable domain with allow-scripts and allow-same-origin and a worker script carrying its own CSP header.

flags.claim: City of Vancouver open-data licence text and attribution rules for datasets other modules may import.
flags.detail: The vancouver.ca terms page (https://vancouver.ca/your-government/terms-of-use.aspx) and the open-data licence page could not be read (HTTP 403 or no licence text). Needs a manual check before any dataset is redistributed.

flags.claim: Whether the VTC brief PDF, site plan and 3D model may be redistributed inside the registry.
flags.detail: Terms 7.5.5 bar redistribution of the Presentation Template Package only; they say nothing about the brief, site plan or model, and the download sits behind an email form. Policy until clarified: link and cite only, do not host.

flags.claim: What counts as 'previously published' under VTC terms 4.1 (a private link, a public repository, a social post), and whether sharing work-in-progress visuals before results is penalised.
flags.detail: 4.1 says visual materials must not have been previously published; the FAQ and resubmission page allow reuse of a concept with visually updated materials; no clause on social media. Ask Buildner support before enabling any public sharing; until then the publish gate stays on.

flags.claim: Who qualifies as an expert reviewer for the expert-reviewed badge, and who stands behind it (UBC SALA faculty, practitioners, a named panel).
flags.detail: Needs a governance decision with the course team; rOpenSci and JOSS show the process but not a qualification standard.

flags.claim: Indigenous governance route: Nation-authorised involvement for content touching Musqueam, Squamish or Tsleil-Waututh knowledge; OCAP (FNIGC) and the City of Vancouver UNDRIP Strategy pages.
flags.detail: OCAP (https://fnigc.ca/ocap/) and the City UNDRIP page (https://vancouver.ca/people-programs/undrip.aspx) returned 403; no Nation-specific protocol was found. CARE (Carroll et al.) and BC's DRIPA were opened. An advisory route via UBC SALA is proposed but unconfirmed; until agreed, such content is held.

flags.claim: Owner of the Layer 0 schema (units, site frame or CRS, grid-to-true-north angle, program tag enum) and the deprecation policy for versioned port types.
flags.detail: Every port type references Layer 0, but no packet is named as its owner in this packet's inputs; P15-M01 only defines the versioning rule. Needs a decision by the data/interoperability owner and the maintainers.

flags.claim: UBC privacy impact and data-residency check for any future server-side storage of projects or comments (GitHub is US-hosted).
flags.detail: Not checked this round; the local-first default avoids server storage of designs, so the check is deferred until a server option is proposed.

unresolved_relationships: Graph size (node and edge count) vs canvas frame time and recompute time in React Flow: the performance guide gives no figures; needs a benchmark.
Pyodide package set and cold-start time vs user abandonment: no sourced numbers; measure first and warm loads.
Number of expert reviewers vs defect escape rate for community modules: rOpenSci uses two but gives no evidence of the optimum.
Rating count and Wilson score vs actual module correctness: the statistic handles sampling uncertainty only; no source links crowd ratings to correctness.
Review response time vs contributor retention in a student-run registry: CHAOSS names the objective but gives no numeric relationship.
Sandbox permission granularity vs contributor and user friction: no sourced evidence.
Auto-run vs manual run vs step-into mode vs user trust in results: no sourced evidence.
Template granularity (nodes per template) vs reuse and learning: no sourced evidence.
Disabled-node mode (bypass vs block) vs correctness of downstream verdicts: design logic only, not empirically sourced.
Effect of COEP require-corp or credentialless on third-party embeds (giscus, map tiles) and on Pyodide interrupts: not verified.
Canvas zoom level vs rendered handle size (React Flow minZoom default 0.5): inferred that handles shrink with the viewport transform; needs measurement against WCAG 2.5.8.
Minimum CSP that QuickJS-WASM and Pyodide need to start (wasm-unsafe-eval alone vs unsafe-eval): not found in the sources read; settle in the CI denial suite.
Whether an opaque-origin sandboxed iframe can start a blob Worker in Chromium, Firefox and WebKit: inferred, not verified.
Cross-engine numeric differences in module outputs vs the tolerance needed per metric type: ECMAScript allows approximation but no sourced magnitudes.
Output size and list-length caps vs memory exhaustion or rendering freeze: no sourced figures; benchmark.
Graph size vs RunRecord size and export time: no sourced figures.
Whether sharing work-in-progress visuals (private link, public repository, social post) counts as 'previously published' under VTC 4.1: terms undefined; ask Buildner.
Time from vulnerability report to client-side block vs exposure of users with the module in their lockfiles: no sourced benchmark.
Local-first storage eviction and clearing vs risk of losing a design: MDN says clearing site data deletes OPFS; no sourced eviction rates.
CRDT collaboration relay (signalling or sync server) vs exposure of unpublished designs: Yjs notes signalling servers; no analysis of confidentiality options.
